newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timorese leave Austrian mission after agreement.
newsitem.headline: Timorese leave Austrian mission after agreement.

text.p: Thirty-three East Timorese youths who entered the Austrian embassy in Jakarta this week as part of a protest left the mission early on Thursday after an agreement with senior Indonesian government officials.
"It was solved at 5.00 a.m. in the morning. Everything went peacefully and in a humanitarian way," Austrian Ambassador Hans Demel told Reuters.

"They went out of the embassy and went down the street and they went into a (police) bus. It was the 28th of the embassy cases and it was a routine case," Demel said, adding he did not know where they had been taken.
Neither the metropolitian police spokesman's office, the International Committee of the Red Cross nor the legal aid lawyers representing the men could immediately confirm their whereabouts.

Demel said the agreement with senior officials of the Indonesian Department of Foreign Affairs stipulated the names of the youths would be taken down and then they would be released based on a similar protest in 1995 at the Dutch embassy.

Police held about 50, mostly East Timorese, protesters in the December 1995 incident for 24 hours before they were released. A similiar number who simultaneously entered the Russian embassy were held for the same amount of time.
Demel said he expected them to be released in " a couple of hours."

Indonesia's armed forces spokesman Brigadier-General Slamet Supriadi was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying on Wednesday that the actions of the youths, who climbed over the embassy's fence, were improper.
"Those who have scaled the embassy fence will be questioned by police once they leave the mission's yard," Supriadi said.

The youths entered the embassy compound on Tuesday afternoon and demanded to meet Jamsheed Marker, the U.N. secretary-general's special envoy on East Timor who is in Jakarta as a part of a familiarisation trip to Indonesia and East Timor.
Only hours after the break-in, three of the youths were taken to meet Marker at United Nations offices in Jakarta.
About 40 youths staged a counter-protest outside the embassy on Wednesday, denouncing the youths inside, witnesses said.
Marker said after a meeting with Indonesia's official National Commission on Human Rights that he had met the youths.
"I took their representation which I will give to the secretary-general," he told reporters.
Since September 1995, 108 East Timorese have entered foreign embassies in Jakarta and asked for political asylum, always granted by Portugal, the former colonial ruler of East Timor.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
